result:
I changed nothing this run. Four FEBio runs are going and nothing else is waiting in either queue, so most of the machine is idle.

- **Resources:** 9 of our 32 CPU cores in use, memory 57 / 128 GB, no out-of-memory kills. None of the 7 GPUs are ours; other users have them all. Disk has 1.5 TB free.
- **Old FEBio queue:** 4 running (physrotFr2 p060, p062, p109, p125, since 15:01), 0 waiting, 2268 done, 2 failed (both old). Only 1 run finished in the last 3 h (16:40). The 4 logs were updated 3–10 s before the check, and their CPU core sets don't overlap.
- **New task queue:** 0 waiting, 0 running, 1 done, 5 failed (the old gate2 tasks from 10-28).
- **Services:** all 6 tmux sessions are up. All running work restarts from its checkpoint, so `resume_all.sh` needs no change.
- **One problem, p109:** its flexion window failed at the start of the dynamic run. The split runner then retried it as static, which got stuck at t=3.55. After 45 min the watchdog stopped it at 19:14, which is the designed behaviour. The extension window now looks the same: 0 steps done after 7 min. That may cost about another hour on 4 cores. Whether this case needs a different setting is a science decision, so I left it alone.
- **What's limiting us:** there isn't enough queued work. 23 cores and about 70 GB of memory are idle, and no scheduling setting can fix that.

Requests in `status.json`:
- Queue more work; all 32 cores will be free once the 4 physrotFr2 runs end.
- Have the science owner look at the p109 stall.
- Still waiting on decisions: T01, T16, T10 (disk guard for the old scheduler) and the al_loop gate.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261102_1926.md
- status.json

I also added one line to `work/ops/foreman_actions.log`.
